title: v0.13.1
excerpt: Added 🦾 Coding agents as models. On an Open Terminal that offers agents, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi now appear in the model picker. You can chat with them or call them by voice, choose their reasoning effort and service tier, and approve their tool requests in the chat. Each conversation uses one agent, and agent chats cannot be regenerated, continued or edited and resent. If an agent's terminal goes away, its chats and new chats fall back to the default model and earlier replies keep the agent's name. Autocompletion in agent chats uses the task model, or is skipped when there is none. #33843 , #33860 , #33880 , #33857 🪢 Introducing Tether. Tether is the new desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that ties your own computer to Open WebUI. Sign in once and your computer shows up under Your devices in the terminal menu, so models, coding agents and automations can work in your real files, repositories and tools, and you can reach them from any browser, including your phone. Tether connects out to Open WebUI, so there are no ports to open, its terminal output resumes after a dropped connection, and it delivers notifications to your desktop even when no Open WebUI page is open. It signs in with a renewable session that expires after 90 days without use by default, set with "SESSION_EXPIRES_IN". 💸 Much cheaper tool chats. Chats that use tools now cost much less.
